population.note: FICTIONAL. Out of about 276M adults, 29.9% are current users (≈82.5M) and 44.0% have ever used (≈121.4M). That leaves 14.1% (≈38.9M) who used and are off now, and ≈154.6M who have never used. Cycling arithmetic: ever 44.0 − current 29.9 = 14.1 pts off now. About 16.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.5 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (16.5 + 5.5)/44.0 = 50.0% have cycled. That fits the parent's ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Ever-use rose 4.0 pts (limit 4.4) because $39–69 generic pens brought in new starters, mostly in the bottom and middle thirds. Current use rose only 1.4 pts, and the gap is friction. Generics mostly replaced gray-market and branded supply rather than adding users (imports fell from ≈7.1M to ≈2.7M). Stopping also rose: after the 2035 randomised anhedonia data, the 2036 Novo document scandal, the NAION warning and the backlash, more people quit or took long holidays. Age check: 18–29: 17% × 52M = 8.8M; 30–49: 34% × 92M = 31.3M; 50–64: 44% × 61M = 26.8M; 65+: 22% × 71M = 15.6M. Total ≈ 82.6M ≈ 29.9%. Income thirds: (31 + 30.5 + 28.2)/3 = 29.9. The bottom-third gap narrowed from 7.5 to 2.8 pts because of generic price and the Medicaid generic option. The top third fell 1 pt as 'unmedicated' and long holidays gained status among professionals. The 65+ band grew slowly because about one older ever-user in five is on a bone pause or a post-NAION stop. Pediatric use is 0.8% of ≈73M ≈ 584k, down from 730k. The 2035 adolescent bone readout and fifteen state age laws pushed it down, and generics did not reverse that. About two children in five still live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it. The never-user group (≈154.6M) is skewed toward under-30s, people with contraindications, refusers by conviction, and a newly visible group of religious and 'whole appetite' refusers in the Upper South.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Public programmes are now the largest payer, at 41.0% of fills. Medicare: the permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays $199/month for branded incretins with a $50 copay. Generic semaglutide joined Part D formularies in late 2035 at plan-negotiated rates of ≈$38 with $0–10 copays. Medicare covers ≈17.0M users (≈15.6M aged 65+ and ≈1.4M disabled under-65), or 20.6% of fills: ≈7.0M for diabetes and ≈10.0M for obesity. About 45% of Medicare users (≈7.65M) are on generic. Gross: 7.65M × $38 × 12 ≈ $3.5B, plus 9.35M × $199 × 12 ≈ $22.3B, ≈ $25.8B in total. That is down from $34.4B in 2034 even though there are 2.6M more users. Medicaid: the Jan 2036 Medicaid Metabolic Generic Option extends the 90% match to any state that covers generic semaglutide first under the CMS continuation standard. Nine states joined, so 40 states plus DC now cover. Medicaid covers ≈16.8M users, or 20.4% of fills, about 75% of them on generic. Gross: 12.6M × $32 × 12 ≈ $4.8B, plus 4.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $10.0B, ≈ $14.9B in total (≈$13.4B federal at 90%), down from $27.5B. Public total ≈ 33.8M users and ≈ $40.7B gross.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ brands at $5–30/month. Three Indian firms (not the Telangana first filer, which is still under import alert) now hold US ANDA approvals and ship legitimately. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide copies, with 'research' retatrutide still the core of the remaining gray trade. Canada: CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt: generics.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The price collapsed for semaglutide only. Seven generic injectable semaglutide ANDAs plus a Novo authorised generic sell at $39–69 cash at warehouse clubs, Cost Plus-style pharmacies and grocery pharmacies, with PBM net ≈$30–40. Tirzepatide and later molecules have no generic. Branded prices: Novo cut branded semaglutide pens to $199 direct and the 50 mg Wegovy pill to $179. Oral starters (Wegovy pill low dose, Foundayo) stay at $149–150 on the portal. Tirzepatide is $279 direct, retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list, amycretin $499, MariTide $549. Payer mix of ≈82.5M users: Medicare 20.6% (17.0M); Medicaid 20.4% (16.8M); commercial 30.9% (25.5M); cash/direct 24.8% (20.5M, including ≈3.6M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers and ≈7.5M generic cash buyers, many on employer reference-price stipends); imported/counterfeit 3.3% (2.7M). Sum = 82.5M = 100%. Roughly 30M users (36%) are on generic semaglutide. Employer coverage fell to 59% because many firms replaced plan coverage with $40–60 monthly HSA stipends. Covering plans are mostly generic-first, and tenure gates are now found in about a fifth of them, since $40 is not worth gating. Routes: ≈41% daily oral, ≈55% weekly injectable, ≈4% monthly. Cheap generic pens slowed the shift to pills even as the pill's price fell. US incretin market ≈$137B: ≈30M generic users × $40 × 12 ≈ $14.4B, plus ≈49.8M branded paying users × ≈$205 × 12 ≈ $122.5B. That is down from ≈$170B.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; no generic)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide incl. 12 mg)

GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide; MASH indication added 2035)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)

mainstream_offlabel_uses: gambling-disorder treatment with low-dose oral semaglutide, endorsed by a 2036 addiction-medicine consensus statement and paid for by problem-gambling funds in New Jersey, Ohio and Michigan, with an sNDA pending
compulsive shopping and compulsive sexual behaviour, prescribed in psychiatry practices, citing the gambling trials
'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (≈3.6M, down from 4.6M), now restricted in fifteen states
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial enrolled, no readout)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
microdosing generic semaglutide pens for 'calm' to avoid subscription fees
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse: on the mid-2035 settlement date FDA declared the Telangana first filer's 180-day exclusivity forfeited, because it had failed to obtain approval within the statutory window while under the warning letter. Seven ANDAs and a Novo authorised generic then launched. Tirzepatide exclusivity runs later. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Sep 2035. Compulsion driver: per the approval rules this is realised as a filing, not an approval. Two randomised trials of 14 mg oral semaglutide in gambling disorder (Copenhagen-led and US academic, Novo co-funded) read out in mid-2035: 38% vs 19% achieved remission of DSM gambling disorder at 26 weeks. They were also the first randomised low-dose SHAPS measurement, with 9% vs 4% clinically meaningful anhedonia. Novo filed an sNDA in Oct 2035 under priority review. The FDA advisory committee in Jun 2036 voted 9–6 for efficacy and asked for anhedonia labelling. A decision is expected early 2037 and is complicated by the document scandal. Oral parity: the 50 mg Wegovy pill (16.4%, matching injectable semaglutide) is the existing product. Lilly filed an NDA for its next-generation oral GLP-1/GIP small molecule in Aug 2036 (≈19% at 72 weeks); it is not approved. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. No compulsion indication is on any US label at the end of 2036.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Generic pen starters with less clinical contact report more early vomiting from fast self-titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; ileus labelled.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (litigation tier)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now mass-tort scale. About 88,000 claims are consolidated in the federal GLP-1 GI/pancreatic MDL in Pennsylvania, up from ≈15,000 in 2034, driven by plaintiff advertising to a 121M ever-user pool and by the Mar 2036 unsealed documents. Epidemiology still shows a modest relative increase in gastroparesis diagnoses. Whether it persists after stopping remains disputed. Plaintiffs who switched to generic are largely barred from suing generic makers by preemption, so claims concentrate on brand-era exposure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: After the unsealing, FDA ordered Novo to resubmit its complete pooled GI safety analyses and opened a class labelling review on post-discontinuation gastroparesis. The first bellwether, in Oct 2036, ended in a $38M plaintiff verdict, now on appeal.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute numbers with the larger user base and the 65+ population.
Still no causal confirmation and low absolute risk. It is now the second-largest claim category in the MDL. Counterfeit confounding is smaller as imports fall.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Part of the FDA review triggered by the Novo resubmission order. No change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈1.9M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Generic users with no coaching show losses at the untrained end, ~35–40% lean.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label. Body-composition monitoring stays in the high-efficacy labels. CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.2M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.2M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 17,200 excess hip fractures a year. The vertebral tail among postmenopausal women 50–64 who cycle continues but has flattened slightly as generic supply cuts forced stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints required in filings. CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged. The DOJ civil case against Novo settled in Nov 2035 for $1.9B with a corporate integrity agreement and no admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4/100,000 baseline among ≈82.5M users, that is ≈2,300 excess cases a year, mostly partial permanent monocular loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034, not boxed. Generic labels carry it. The NAION MDL is in discovery.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the 2035 gambling trials found none.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now has its first randomised low-dose data: 9% vs 4% SHAPS-defined anhedonia at 14 mg oral semaglutide in the 2035 gambling trials, alongside the 2032 observational ~12% vs ~5% at 12 mg retatrutide. Applied crudely to ≈3.6M low-dose 'calm' subscribers, that is ≈180k excess cases if it generalises. Dose holidays are widespread and self-managed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The advisory committee asked for an anhedonia statement in any compulsion label. FDA has opened class labelling discussions with no change yet. FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Forced stops for price and supply fell as generics arrived. Voluntary stops after the scandal, the backlash and holidays rose. Net off-now pool is 38.9M.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code. Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules still in force.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated in generic cash users with no counselling and in high-loss older users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D counselling template screens for it. Medicaid generic option requires the same screening. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent bone readout showed ≈3% lower lumbar BMD accrual at two years than controls, partly recovering after stopping. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent labelling updated with bone monitoring. Fifteen states use the readout to justify age laws. Postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Shrinking. Imports and counterfeits fell from ≈7.1M to ≈2.7M users, now mostly 'research' retatrutide and tirzepatide copies, because generic semaglutide undercuts parcels. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are down ~35% from the 2034 peak and still above 2032. No contamination cluster on the 2033 scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts stand. The Safe Pens bill is still stalled. Individuals are not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistent in the 'calm' tablet niche, especially in the fifteen restriction states where telehealth subscriptions were cut off. Seized lots contain 0–300% of label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ long-term users, with NAION a cofactor in a minority.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New cases from forced stops are fewer. The existing cohort, women 50–64 who cycled 2031–34, carries the pattern forward.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035 recommending resistance training before any planned stop; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New. Cash generic buyers with only a pharmacist consult escalate too fast or mistake multi-dose pen clicks. This drives GI ED visits and a minority of hypoglycaemia cases in insulin users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA asked ANDA holders for harmonised titration cards. Medicaid generic option requires a starting visit; cash channels do not.

food_and_beverage.state: With ~30% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~3% a year and confectionery ~4%, a slower decline as stops and holidays rise. Discount grocers' 'regain-friendly' value packs lost ground in Dayton and west Phoenix as cheap generics cut forced cycling. Premium protein still leads. A small 'whole appetite' food segment of heritage baking, lard-and-butter brands and church cookbooks is growing in Tennessee and Kentucky.

alcohol.state: Eighth straight year of spirits decline, with beer also down. Non-alcoholic formats hold. The new adjacent loser is gaming: sportsbook handle growth in New Jersey and Ohio has slowed below trend, and operators quietly fund 'responsible gaming' research rather than oppose state problem-gambling funds paying for semaglutide.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat. Spend per cover is still ~10% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. 'Holiday weekend' menus aimed at diners off the drug for two days are standard on Friday and Saturday in Nashville and Atlanta. Value buffets in the Upper South are stabilising.

apparel.state: 'Structured' and 'cycle' ranges persist, but the cycle range sells less as generic users stay on. Resale sized for cycling plateaus. Plus sizes return to mid-market racks in the Southeast, marketed with backlash language.

fitness.state: Growing more slowly. DEXA-plus-coaching chains keep adding sites and Medicare Advantage prescribed lifting expands. Medicaid generic-option states fund group strength classes in a few pilots. The staff bottleneck for older lifters remains.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% as generics replaced branded semaglutide. Employers moved to generic-first formularies or $40–60 HSA stipends. Kiosk-weight premium tiers survive, and tenure gates fade because the drug is no longer worth gating. Life insurers still price untreated BMI. Product-liability reserves at Novo's insurers became a 2036 earnings item.

pharma.state: US incretin revenue fell from ≈$170B to ≈$137B even with more users. Novo is hit three times: generics took its molecule, it paid the $1.9B DOJ settlement, and it carries the MDL documents. It defends with the $179 pill and amycretin. Lilly is less exposed, protected by tirzepatide and retatrutide exclusivity and its oral filing. Indian generic makers gained legitimate US share.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Still income, but the signal has blurred. Generic pens at $49 ended most forced cycling in the bottom third, so a lean body tells you less. Shape still sorts people: coached DEXA-verified muscle at the top, a soft 'generic body' with thin arms in the middle and bottom. A new third signal is deliberate, visible fullness among women under 35 in the Upper South, worn as a stance.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use gaps narrowed (31% top, 28.2% bottom) and the result gap did not. Women 50–64 who cycled during 2031–34 still carry fat-dominant regain and the vertebral-fracture tail. In Phoenix, Maryvale users now get pens from a Fry's pharmacy instead of a parcel, and their DEXA results still look like Maryvale's.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals remain the user default. Weekend 'holiday' dinners have become a ritual of their own. Hosts ask whether guests are 'on, off, or holiday' and cook Saturday for appetite. In Nashville and Knoxville, 'Whole Appetite' Sunday potlucks at Baptist and nondenominational churches run as explicit counter-programming.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list 'on / off / holiday weekends'. 'Unmedicated' has grown from a niche into a recognisable type among under-30s, especially women. 'Generic' versus 'coached' still reads as income. Some users ask about a partner's gambling prescription the way they once asked about antidepressants.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. The insured still treat appetite as managed. A visible backlash coalition has formed: a fat-acceptance revival on short video led by women under 35, evangelical preaching that 'appetite is a gift' after a Southern Baptist resolution in 2035, and an anti-pharma wing energised by the Novo documents. It is loud in Tennessee, Kentucky and Oklahoma and remains a minority nationally.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Randomised low-dose data now exist: 9% vs 4% anhedonia at 14 mg oral semaglutide in the 2035 gambling trials. The 12 mg retatrutide observational figures (~12% vs ~5%) still apply to ≈8.5M people on top-dose triple or dual regimens, ≈600k excess cases if causal. Among ≈3.6M 'calm' subscribers, ≈180k excess cases if the trial rate generalises. Surveys suggest about a third of current users take planned dose holidays at least monthly, usually skipping a weekly dose or pausing the pill for a weekend.
interior_life.framing: A side effect again, and a thing you complain about. 'The grey' is a phrase used in sitcoms and primary-care visits. 'Holiday' is a verb. Prescribers still say 'reward modulation'. The same mechanism is the pitch for the pending gambling indication, and nobody has resolved that.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Most large employers dropped 'focus' subscriptions from lifestyle catalogues after the restriction laws and the trial data, citing liability. Sales and hospitality staff still dose down before peaks, and 'Friday holiday' is common in white-collar offices. Some managers now treat 'are you on holiday this week?' as a question about mood. Tenure-gate bargaining faded once generics made gating pointless.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' is a mainstream joke. A 2036 network comedy about a couple who schedule their holidays is a hit. Comics who wrote 'unmedicated' as a niche badge now headline. In New Jersey and Ohio, recovery groups for problem gamblers split over whether people on semaglutide are 'really sober'.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely plan intimacy around holiday weekends. Couples fight over asymmetry: one partner on holiday and vivid, the other on and even. Partners of men prescribed for gambling report relief and flatness at once.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: An odd coalition. The Medicaid generic option passed with bipartisan votes as a cost saver. The restriction laws (age floors, a ban on asynchronous telehealth prescribing for non-approved uses, outdoor ad bans) passed mostly in Republican-led Upper South legislatures with backlash, church and anti-pharma support, plus some Democratic votes on child protection. The Novo documents are campaign material in 2036. Plaintiff firms are major donors.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is enforcing and cautious. It declared the first filer's exclusivity forfeited and approved seven generics. It approved survodutide for MASH and ordered Novo to resubmit its full GI safety analyses. It is moving slowly on the gambling sNDA and on anhedonia labelling. Congress has still passed no importation or authentication law. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Public expansion. The Jan 2036 Medicaid Metabolic Generic Option extends the 90% match to generic-first coverage under the existing continuation standard, and 40 states plus DC now cover. Generic semaglutide is in Part D at ≈$38 with $0–10 copays beside the unchanged $199/$50 branded benefit. Public programmes pay 41% of fills and are the largest payer. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: CMS continuation standard unchanged: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, 90-day bone-pause code, two misses suspend for 6 months. It now covers ≈34M public users. Indiana and Arkansas keep 12-month rules, and the Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver in 2035. Private kiosk-weight premium tiers persist. The restriction states require in-person visits for minors and for non-approved uses, which creates a new paper trail.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Large fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. The Army now accepts recruits on generic semaglutide with 12 months' stable weight, a quiet change made because generics are cheap to continue. Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US–India irritant eased because Indian firms now sell generics into the US legally, though the Telangana first filer remains under import alert. Generic semaglutide is exempted from the Section 232 tariffs in the 2036 law. Chinese API underlies both legal generics and the residual gray trade in retatrutide.

events.event: FDA declares the first filer's 180-day exclusivity on semaglutide forfeited as rival filers' settlement dates arrive, and seven generic injectable semaglutide products plus a Novo authorised generic launch. Warehouse-club cash prices hit $49 within ten weeks, and Novo cuts its branded pen to $199 and the 50 mg pill to $179

Tennessee enacts an age-18 floor for incretin prescribing outside specialist care, a ban on asynchronous telehealth prescribing for unapproved uses such as 'calm', and an outdoor-advertising ban, citing the adolescent bone readout. Fourteen more states copy at least two of the three provisions by late 2036, and a federal court enjoins the ad ban in Kentucky

Novo files for a gambling-disorder indication for oral semaglutide after two randomised trials show remission doubling. The same trials give the first randomised low-dose anhedonia figure, 9% versus 4%, and 'the grey' moves from forum slang to network sitcom

Congress passes the Medicaid Metabolic Generic Option in a health extenders package, scored as saving money at generic prices. Nine more states join within months, and Medicare and Medicaid together become the largest payer for the drugs

Documents unsealed in the federal GLP-1 gastrointestinal litigation show Novo safety staff held back a 2022 pooled analysis of severe gastroparesis from a periodic FDA safety report. Novo's chief medical officer resigns, FDA orders a full resubmission, and claims in the litigation pass 88,000 by October, when the first bellwether jury awards $38M

Lilly files for approval of a next-generation oral GLP-1/GIP pill at about 19% weight loss, chasing tirzepatide-level results without a needle. Daily pills reach 41% of users even as $49 generic pens pull the price-sensitive back to injections

open_tensions: The gambling indication and the grey are the same signal. FDA must decide in early 2037 whether to approve a compulsion indication with an anhedonia statement, while fifteen states ban telehealth prescribing for exactly that kind of unapproved use and Novo's credibility is at its lowest point.

Mass-tort exposure is concentrated on brand-era use. Generic users are largely barred from suing by preemption, so 88,000 claims and the Novo documents press on a company whose molecule is now a $49 commodity, and plaintiff firms are canvassing a 121M ever-user pool.

Public programmes are the default payer at generic prices and the cost curve fell. The 2036 savings score counts the cheaper drug but not ≈17,200 excess hip fractures a year, ≈2,300 NAION cases, or sarcopenia care billed to Part A and Medicare Advantage, and tirzepatide and retatrutide remain a branded upper tier.

The backlash won laws but not the national body. Age floors and ad bans face court challenges, adolescent use is falling while adolescent obesity is not, and the 'Whole Appetite' movement's growth among women under 35 in the Upper South is the first sustained drop in uptake in any group.
still_true: The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate for branded incretins with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, the 90-day 'bone pause' code, two misses suspend for 6 months).
Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) has no US generic, and retatrutide still lists at $1,649/month.
The FTC consent orders on 'calm' and 'focus' brands stand: no 'anxiety treatment' claims.
The NAION class Warnings and Precautions statement is on every GLP-1 receptor agonist label and is not boxed.

prose.headline: The $49 Pen: Generic Semaglutide Is Here, Medicaid Pays, Novo Is in Court, and America Is Taking Weekends Off From the Grey
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 three American adults in ten are on an incretin drug, a little more than two years ago. The flat headline number hides a lot of movement. The molecule most of them take is now a commodity. In June 2035 the FDA ruled that the company holding the first right to sell generic semaglutide had lost it by sitting under a warning letter too long. Seven generics and Novo's own authorised version launched within weeks, and by late summer a month of pens cost forty-nine dollars at a warehouse club. Novo cut its brand to $199 and its fifty-milligram pill to $179. Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide kept their patents and their prices, so the market split into a cheap floor and a coached ceiling.

The parcel trade mostly dried up. Seven million Americans had been injecting Indian pens and Chinese vials. Now fewer than three million do, mostly bodybuilders chasing retatrutide doses no generic offers. Poison-centre calls are falling for the first time in years.

Cheap drugs turned Washington's arithmetic upside down. A Congress that had argued for a decade about what obesity drugs cost passed a Medicaid generic option in January as a savings measure. Nine more states joined, and forty plus DC now cover. Medicare added generic semaglutide at about thirty-eight dollars a month beside the statutory $199 brand benefit, which nobody touched. Public programmes now pay for more fills than employers do. Many employers stopped covering the drug and started handing workers fifty dollars a month to buy it themselves. Medicare and Medicaid together spend less on these drugs than in 2034 while covering several million more people. The bone fractures, about seventeen thousand excess hip fractures a year, are still billed to a different part of Medicare and are still left out of the savings estimates.

The number of users did not jump because stopping became normal too. In the autumn of 2035 two randomised trials showed that low-dose oral semaglutide doubled remission in gambling disorder. In the same pages they gave the first controlled measurement of what users had called the grey: nine percent anhedonia against four on placebo. Novo filed for the indication anyway. The advisory committee voted narrowly for it and asked for a warning about pleasure. A decision is due in 2037. Meanwhile 'holiday' has become a verb. About a third of users skip a dose or a weekend of pills each month to feel things, and restaurants in Nashville and Atlanta now run Friday menus for them.

Then in March the gastrointestinal lawsuits produced documents. Unsealed files showed Novo's safety staff had held back a 2022 pooled analysis of severe gastroparesis from a regulatory report. The chief medical officer resigned and the FDA demanded everything again. Claims passed eighty-eight thousand, and the first jury awarded thirty-eight million dollars. Most people who now take generic semaglutide cannot sue anyone. Federal preemption shields generic makers, so the liability stays tied to the years when there was only one brand.

The backlash has an address. In Tennessee, after an adolescent bone study found slower growth in bone density, the legislature set an age floor for prescribing, banned telehealth 'calm' subscriptions and banned billboards. Fourteen states have copied parts of it, and a court has blocked the billboard ban in Kentucky. Baptist congregations host Whole Appetite potlucks. Young women post their fullness on short video as a stance, and among women under thirty-five in the Upper South uptake is falling for the first time anywhere. Nationally they are a minority. Most Americans who want the drug can now afford it. The open questions are what it costs them and who will be held responsible.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Pruitt sets the alarm for 5:10 and checks the fridge door first. The pen is on the butter shelf, a white generic with a Hyderabad lot number she no longer bothers to look up. Forty-nine dollars at the Kroger pharmacy on Clinton Highway. The school district gives her fifty a month for it in an HSA, so she makes a dollar.

It's Thursday, injection day, but she doesn't. Saturday is her mother's seventieth, and Dana wants to taste the coconut cake.

At the middle-school cafeteria she runs the line: grilled chicken, green beans, a roll most kids leave. Three eighth-grade girls in Whole Appetite T-shirts eat every roll on the tray, loudly. Dana says nothing. Her own daughter, Kayleigh, fifteen, is on a waitlist for a pediatric endocrinologist in Nashville, because Tennessee doesn't let the family doctor prescribe to her anymore. The wait is eleven weeks.

After work Dana drives Ray to his appointment. He goes in person now; the law says he has to. Fourteen milligrams, oral, for the betting. He hasn't opened the app since March. He also hasn't laughed at the Vols game since March, and they both notice it.

'You're skipping,' he says in the truck, not asking.

'Till Sunday.'

He nods. He'd skip too if he could. The doctor told him that's the one thing he shouldn't do.

That night a lawyer's ad runs between innings: Were you on Ozempic before 2035? Dana was, for two years, back when the plan paid. She writes the phone number on the grocery list, under eggs.
